newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch says c/a deterioration not unexpected.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch says c/a deterioration not unexpected.

text.p: Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Friday the deterioration of New Zealand's current account deficit "was not unexpectedly slightly above forecast".
The March quarter deficit swelled to NZ$4.5 billion, 4.8 percent of GDP, from $3.8 billion at December 31, which was well ahead of the market forecast of $4.1 billion.
"GDP figures have already shown the economy experienced a weak start to the year," Birch said in a statement.
He said the result was broadly consistent with Treasury's forecast of a deterioration.
He said it was important to recognise that the government was a net saver and not contributing to the current account deficit.
Transactions in the account reflected rational business decision by the private sector, Birch said.
"Borrowing overseas by New Zealand businesses, for example, will reflect productive use of an asset or other investment.
"This is why the ratings agencies which judge New Zealand's creditworthiness are not concerned about the balance of payments deficit."
Birch added that Treasury was forecasting a slight improvement in the deficit in 1999/2000.
